join_order.probe: num(filtered uom='USD' AND value IS NOT NULL, ~33.3M rows)
join_order.notes: Build dense sub_info array indexed by adsh_code; O(1) lookup per num row combines join check + attribute fetch

sub_info_array.description: Array indexed by adsh_code, stores {uint32_t name_code, int32_t cik} for qualifying sub rows, sentinel (UINT32_MAX) for non-qualifying

cik_agg_map.notes: For HAVING subquery; computed in same pass as main aggregation

parallelism.merge_phase: serial merge of thread-local maps (small — ~15K entries per map)
parallelism.notes: 64 threads * (360KB + 240KB) = ~38MB per-thread maps fit in 44MB LLC

indexes.purpose: Map adsh_code -> sub_row_id during sub_info_array construction
indexes.usage: NOT used during num scan; sub_info_array replaces it for O(1) combined filter+lookup

map1.purpose: main query GROUP BY (name_code, cik) -> SUM(value)

map2.purpose: HAVING subquery GROUP BY cik -> SUM(value)

aggregation.having_computation: After merge: iterate cik_agg_map, compute sum_of_sums / count -> avg_threshold
aggregation.having_filter: Keep main_agg_map entries where sum_value > avg_threshold

output.decode: Resolve name_code -> string via dictionaries/name.dict for output

num_scan.scan_order: Check uom first (uint16_t, cheapest), then value_null (uint8_t), then adsh lookup in sub_info_array, then read value (double) only for qualifying rows
num_scan.notes: demand-paged mmap without MAP_POPULATE; exclude munmap from timing via RAII scoping

optimization_notes.single_pass: Main query and HAVING subquery share identical base scan — accumulate both maps simultaneously
optimization_notes.filter_ordering: uom check (uint16_t compare) → value_null check (uint8_t) → sub_info_array lookup (combined join + fy filter) → read value (double) — ordered by cost, each step eliminates rows
optimization_notes.memory_layout: sub_info_array + all thread-local maps fit comfortably in LLC
